title: Local Response Stability for Certified Two-Step Rollout in Engineering Optimization
abstract_tex: Two-step rollout couples first-action choice to response-dependent continuation. We propose response-stability-guided value enclosures for a finite-menu engineering optimization problem. Decomposing positive-response terminal improvement into a first-evaluation baseline and bounded continuation remainder yields regional selection certificates without identifying every continuation action. Directed posterior and integration bounds control numerical error. A frozen probability-bound implementation verifies matching selections on 43 archived beam-design states. Local stability reduces complete projections from 114 to 25, but takes 5.47 seconds versus 4.93 seconds directly. Subsequent regional postprocessing tightens all 89 fixed-continuation intervals by a median 37.1\%, without model reconstruction or new conditional-reward integration. Choices remain unchanged. Paid engineering replay is mixed. The contribution is a regional value-enclosure mechanism for certified rollout selection under a fixed finite model. Numerical applicability is demonstrated; time savings, engineering-policy superiority and continuous-domain convergence are unestablished.
